title: From Speech to Subtitles: Evaluating ASR Models in Subtitling Italian Television Programs
abstract: arXiv:2512.19161v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Subtitles are essential for video accessibility and audience engagement. Modern Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems, built upon Encoder-Decoder neural network architectures and trained on massive amounts of data, have progressively reduced transcription errors on standard benchmark datasets. However, their performance in real-world production environments, particularly for non-English content like long-form Italian videos, remains largely unexplored. This paper presents a case study on developing a professional subtitling system for an Italian media company. To inform our system design, we evaluated four state-of-the-art ASR models (Whisper Large v2, AssemblyAI Universal, Parakeet TDT v3 0.6b, and WhisperX) on a 50-hour dataset of Italian television programs. translated_title: 从语音到字幕：评估用于意大利电视节目字幕制作的ASR模型
translated_abstract: 字幕对于视频的可访问性和观众参与度至关重要。基于编码器-解码器神经网络架构并在海量数据上训练的现代自动语音识别（ASR）系统，已逐步降低了标准基准数据集上的转录错误。然而，它们在真实生产环境中的表现，尤其是针对意大利语等非英语的长视频内容，在很大程度上仍未被探索。本文介绍了一个为意大利媒体公司开发专业字幕系统的案例研究。为了指导系统设计，我们在一个50小时的意大利电视节目数据集上评估了四个最先进的ASR模型（Whisper Large v2、AssemblyAI Universal、Parakeet TDT v3 0.6b和WhisperX）。该研究通过与专业人工字幕员的工作进行基准对比，突出了这些模型的优势与局限性。研究结果表明，虽然……
tldr: 本研究针对意大利媒体公司的字幕制作需求，在50小时意大利电视节目数据上评估了四个最先进的ASR模型，并与专业人工字幕员的表现进行对比，揭示了它们在真实生产环境中的优势与局限。
en_tdlr: This study benchmarks four state-of-the-art ASR models against professional human subtitlers on a 50-hour dataset of Italian television programs to inform the development of a professional subtitling system for an Italian media company.
